newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Alcatel sees recovery, shares soar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Alcatel sees recovery, shares soar.

text.p: France's largest industrial group, Alcatel Alsthom, promised on Thursday a hefty turnaround for 1996 from record losses the year before, sending its shares soaring on the Paris bourse.

The electrical engineering giant said it expected to post 1996 net income of 2.5 billion francs ($451.7 million) after a 25.6 billion francs loss in 1995 when it had to pay for massive restucturing to adapt to new competition.
Analysts had expected Alcatel to show a 1996 profit closer to 1.4 billion francs. Its final figures are due in March.
Alcatel shares surged by as much as 9.9 percent in heavy early trading on Thursday, helping the blue-chip Paris CAC-40 share index to a record above 2,500 points.
Alcatel's stock hit a high of 497.7 francs, just short of its high for the year of 500 francs, before settling around midday at 492.5 francs, up from 452.7 francs on Wednesday.

"After taking into account exceptional items, and in particular capital gains resulting from the non-strategic asset disposal programme, the group's 1996 net income should amount to approximately 2.5 billion (francs)," Alcatel said in a statement on its provisional profit for 1996.
It said 1996 sales came in at 162.0 billion francs, little changed from 1995, and orders rose eight percent to 168.2 billion, reflecting a pick-up in business activity.

However, the start of a recovery in the telecommunications sector, where Alcatel is a top equipment supplier, would push income from operations to more than 2.7 billion francs in 1996 from less than a quarter of that level, 600 million, in 1995.
"1996 was characterised by a significant flow of contracts in the telecom sector, which was maintained during the last months of the year," Alcatel said.
Its undersea cables division had also achieved various commercial successes at the end of 1996 and in early 1997 after a period of strong slowdown.
Alcatel said its 1996 performance underscored its recovery plans and confirmed the company's target of reaching a "satisfactory level of profitability in 1998".
The 1996 profit would be the first for chairman Serge Tchuruk since he took over an ailing giant with activities as diverse as telecommunications and high-speed trains in 1995.

The group had fallen on hard times during explosive growth in mobile telecommunications and austerity drives by telecoms operators facing new competition and preparing for full liberalisation of the sector after 1998.
Tchuruk slimmed down management, reorganised the company along product lines and initiated a two-pronged programme of cost-cuts and asset sales.

The 1995 loss, France's worst this century, was almost entirely due to exceptional charges of 23.9 billion francs to pay for restructuring. Some 20,000 people have lost their jobs, mainly in Europe, of the 191,000 employed at the end of 1995.
Last September, Alcatel said it had cut its first-half loss to 400 million francs in 1996, from 1.2 billion in the first six months of 1995, and predicted a profit for 1996.
